source.text: Τότε ἔρχεται μετ’ αὐτῶν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς χωρίον λεγόμενον Γεθσημανὶ, καὶ λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς· Καθίσατε αὐτοῦ ἕως οὗ ἀπελθὼν ἐκεῖ προσεύξωμαι.

records.literal_gloss: Then comes with them the Jesus to a place called Gethsemane, and he says to the disciples, Sit here until having gone away there I pray.

en.L: Then Jesus comes with them to a place called Gethsemane, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to the disciples, "Sit here while I go over there and pray."
en.B: Jesus then came with them to a place named Gethsemane. He told the disciples, "Stay seated here while I go on over there and pray."
en.R: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers came to a place called Gethsemane. Jesus said to them, "Stay here. I am going over there to pray."

decisions.choice: Gethsemane: a plot of land on the Mount of Olives
decisions.reason: The name means "oil press". John 18:1 calls it a garden; it was likely an olive grove.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

source.text: καὶ παραλαβὼν τὸν Πέτρον καὶ τοὺς δύο υἱοὺς Ζεβεδαίου ἤρξατο λυπεῖσθαι καὶ ἀδημονεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: And having taken along the Peter and the two sons of Zebedee he began to be sorrowful and to be distressed.

en.L: And taking along Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to be sorrowful and deeply distressed.
en.B: He took Peter and Zebedee's two sons with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to be filled with grief and anguish.
en.R: He took Peter, James, and John with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Jesus began to feel very sad and troubled.

decisions.choice: Peter and the two sons of Zebedee: Peter, James and John
decisions.reason: The same three were with Jesus on the mountain where he was transfigured (17:1). The sons of Zebedee are James and John (4:21).

decisions.choice: deeply distressed: in anguish, overwhelmed
decisions.reason: The word describes deep inner turmoil.

decisions.choice: James, and John
decisions.reason: Readable names the two brothers.

source.text: τότε λέγει αὐτοῖς· Περίλυπός ἐστιν ἡ ψυχή μου ἕως θανάτου· μείνατε ὧδε καὶ γρηγορεῖτε μετ’ ἐμοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Then he says to them, Very sorrowful is the soul of me unto death; remain here and watch with me.

en.L: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "My soul is very sorrowful, even to death; stay here and keep watch with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "My soul is weighed down with grief, even to death. Stay here and keep awake with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.R: He said to them, "My heart is so full of sadness that I feel I could die. Stay here and keep watch with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

decisions.choice: my soul is very sorrowful: Psalms 42-43
decisions.reason: The psalmist asks, "Why are you cast down, my soul?" (Psalm 42:5, 11; 43:5). Jesus uses the psalm's language for his grief.

decisions.choice: even to death: grief so heavy it could kill
alternatives: sorrow because death is near only
decisions.reason: The phrase measures the depth of the grief. Compare Jonah 4:9.

decisions.choice: keep watch: stay awake and alert
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in 24:42 and 25:13 for being ready.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: My heart is so full of sadness that I feel I could die
alternatives: My soul is very sorrowful, even to death
decisions.reason: Readable explains the saying.

source.text: καὶ προελθὼν μικρὸν ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ προσευχόμενος καὶ λέγων· Πάτερ μου, εἰ δυνατόν ἐστιν, παρελθάτω ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ τὸ ποτήριον τοῦτο· πλὴν οὐχ ὡς ἐγὼ θέλω ἀλλ’ ὡς σύ.

records.literal_gloss: And having gone forward a little he fell on face of him praying and saying, Father of me, if possible it is, let pass from me the cup this; yet not as I will but as you.

en.L: And going a little farther, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} fell on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face, praying and saying, "My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; yet not as I will, but as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [will]."
en.B: He went a little farther, threw {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} face down on the ground, and prayed, "My Father, if there is any way, let this cup pass by {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. But not what I want; what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want."
en.R: He went a little farther and lay down with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face on the ground. He prayed, "My Father, if it is possible, do not make {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} drink this cup of suffering. But do what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want, not what I want."

decisions.choice: this cup: the suffering and death before him, as God's judgment on sin
decisions.reason: In the prophets the cup stands for God's anger poured out (Isaiah 51:17; Jeremiah 25:15). Jesus asked James and John whether they could drink his cup (20:22).

decisions.choice: fell on his face: lay face down in deep humility
decisions.reason: Lying face down was a posture of urgent prayer and submission.

decisions.choice: not as I will, but as you will: the verb is supplied from the first half
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves out the second "will". Jesus submits his will to his Father's.

decisions.choice: do not make me drink this cup of suffering
alternatives: let this cup pass from me
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the cup.

source.text: καὶ ἔρχεται πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς καὶ εὑρίσκει αὐτοὺς καθεύδοντας, καὶ λέγει τῷ Πέτρῳ· Οὕτως οὐκ ἰσχύσατε μίαν ὥραν γρηγορῆσαι μετ’ ἐμοῦ;

records.literal_gloss: And he comes to the disciples and finds them sleeping, and says to the Peter, So not you were able one hour to watch with me?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes to the disciples and finds them sleeping, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to Peter, "So, you could not keep watch with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for one hour?
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came back to the disciples and found them asleep. He said to Peter, "So none of you could stay awake with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for even one hour?
en.R: Then Jesus went back to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers and found them sleeping. He said to Peter, "Could you not stay awake with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for just one hour?

decisions.choice: you could not: plural, spoken to Peter for all three
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to Peter, who had boasted (26:33-35), but the verb is plural.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: none of you
decisions.reason: Balanced shows that the "you" is plural.

source.text: γρηγορεῖτε καὶ προσεύχεσθε, ἵνα μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς πειρασμόν· τὸ μὲν πνεῦμα πρόθυμον ἡ δὲ σὰρξ ἀσθενής.

records.literal_gloss: Watch and pray, that not you enter into temptation; the indeed spirit willing, the but flesh weak.

en.L: Keep watch and pray, so that you may not enter into temptation; the spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak."
en.B: Stay alert and pray that you will not come into testing. The spirit is eager, but human nature is weak."
en.R: Stay awake and pray, so that you will not fail when you are tested. Your spirit wants to do what is right, but your human nature is weak."

decisions.choice: temptation: testing, a trial that could lead them to fall away
decisions.reason: As in the Lord's Prayer (6:13). The test that night is whether they will stand by Jesus.

decisions.choice: the spirit and the flesh: the willing human spirit and weak human nature
alternatives: God's Spirit and the human body
decisions.reason: The disciples truly mean their promises (26:35), but they are frail. Some take "spirit" as the Spirit God gives (Psalm 51:12).

decisions.choice: testing (B); fail when you are tested (R)
decisions.reason: As in 6:13, Balanced and Readable use the wider word; Literal keeps the traditional one.

decisions.choice: human nature
decisions.reason: "Flesh" here means human weakness, not the body alone.

source.text: πάλιν ἐκ δευτέρου ἀπελθὼν προσηύξατο λέγων· Πάτερ μου, εἰ οὐ δύναται τοῦτο παρελθεῖν ἐὰν μὴ αὐτὸ πίω, γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου.

records.literal_gloss: Again for a second time having gone away he prayed saying, Father of me, if not is possible this to pass if not it I drink, let be done the will of you.

en.L: Again, for a second time, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went away and prayed, saying, "My Father, if this cannot pass unless I drink it, let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} will be done."
en.B: He went away again, a second time, and prayed: "My Father, if there is no way for this to pass unless I drink it, then let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} will be done."
en.R: Jesus went away a second time and prayed, "My Father, if I must drink this cup of suffering, then let what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want be done."

decisions.choice: let your will be done: the words of the Lord's Prayer
decisions.reason: Jesus prays the words he taught his disciples (6:10).

decisions.choice: this, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: this cup, and from me, in many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "cup" and "from me", as in 26:39. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: if I must drink this cup of suffering
alternatives: if this cannot pass unless I drink it
decisions.reason: Readable states the condition positively and names the cup of 26:39.

source.text: καὶ ἐλθὼν πάλιν εὗρεν αὐτοὺς καθεύδοντας, ἦσαν γὰρ αὐτῶν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ βεβαρημένοι.

records.literal_gloss: And having come again he found them sleeping, were for of them the eyes weighed down.

en.L: And coming again, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.
en.B: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came back, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} again found them asleep; they could not keep their eyes open.
en.R: When Jesus came back, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found them sleeping again. They were too tired to keep their eyes open.

decisions.choice: their eyes were heavy: they were overcome by sleep
decisions.reason: A common way of saying that sleep had overpowered them.

source.text: καὶ ἀφεὶς αὐτοὺς πάλιν ἀπελθὼν προσηύξατο ἐκ τρίτου τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον εἰπὼν πάλιν.

records.literal_gloss: And having left them again having gone away he prayed a third time the same word having said again.

en.L: And leaving them again, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went away and prayed a third time, saying the same word again.
en.B: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left them, went away once more, and prayed a third time, saying the same words.
en.R: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left them and went away again. He prayed a third time, saying the same thing.

decisions.choice: the same word: the same prayer as before
decisions.reason: He prayed again as in 26:42.

source.text: τότε ἔρχεται πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Καθεύδετε τὸ λοιπὸν καὶ ἀναπαύεσθε· ἰδοὺ ἤγγικεν ἡ ὥρα καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται εἰς χεῖρας ἁμαρτωλῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Then he comes to the disciples and says to them, Sleep the rest and take rest; behold, has drawn near the hour and the Son of the Man is handed over into hands of sinners.

en.L: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes to the disciples and says to them, "Sleep on now and take your rest. Look, the hour has drawn near, and the Son of Man is betrayed into [the] hands of sinners.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came to the disciples and said to them, "Go on sleeping, then, and resting. The hour is here: the Son of Man is being betrayed into the hands of sinners.
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came back to the followers and said to them, "Sleep on, then, and rest! But now the time has come. The Son of Man is being handed over to sinners.

decisions.choice: sleep on and rest: a command, spoken with sorrow or irony
alternatives: a question: Are you still sleeping and resting?
decisions.reason: The words can be read as a command or as a question; the SBLGNT punctuation reads them as a statement. Either way Jesus tells them the time for watching is past, and in 26:46 he rouses them.

decisions.choice: the hour: the appointed time of his suffering
decisions.reason: Compare "my time" in 26:18.

decisions.choice: sinners: those who do not keep God's law, here the men coming to arrest him
decisions.reason: The word may also look ahead to the Gentiles to whom he will be handed over (20:19).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

source.text: ἐγείρεσθε ἄγωμεν· ἰδοὺ ἤγγικεν ὁ παραδιδούς με.

records.literal_gloss: Rise, let us go; behold, has drawn near the one handing over me.

en.L: Get up, let us go. Look, the [one] who is betraying {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} has drawn near."
en.B: Get up; let us be going. Here comes the man who is betraying {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.R: Get up! Let us go. The one who is handing {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} over is coming!"

decisions.choice: let us go: go to meet them
decisions.reason: Jesus does not flee; he goes out to face the one who betrays him.

decisions.choice: look (L); here comes (B); not rendered (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

source.text: Καὶ ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἰδοὺ Ἰούδας εἷς τῶν δώδεκα ἦλθεν καὶ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ὄχλος πολὺς μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων ἀπὸ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ πρεσβυτέρων τοῦ λαοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And still of him speaking, behold, Judas one of the twelve came, and with him a crowd great with swords and clubs from the chief priests and elders of the people.

en.L: And while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still speaking, look, Judas, one of the Twelve, came, and with him a large crowd with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and elders of the people.
en.B: Jesus had not finished speaking when Judas, one of the Twelve, came up. A large crowd came with him, carrying swords and clubs. The chief priests and the elders of the people had sent them.
en.R: Jesus was still talking when Judas came. He was one of the twelve followers. A big crowd came with him. They carried swords and wooden clubs. The leading priests and older leaders of the people had sent them.

decisions.choice: a large crowd with swords and clubs: an armed band, probably the temple guard and servants of the chief priests
decisions.reason: They were sent by the chief priests, and the high priest's slave was among them (26:51). John 18:3 also mentions soldiers.

decisions.choice: one of the Twelve: Matthew stresses that the betrayer was one of his own
decisions.reason: Matthew has already told the reader who Judas is (10:4; 26:14). Repeating it here underlines the betrayal.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: the chief priests had sent them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "from" means.

source.text: ὁ δὲ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς σημεῖον λέγων· Ὃν ἂν φιλήσω αὐτός ἐστιν· κρατήσατε αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] and handing over him gave them a sign saying, Whom ever I kiss, he is; seize him.

en.L: Now the [one] betraying {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} had given them a sign, saying, "Whomever I kiss, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is [the one]; seize {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.B: The betrayer had given them a sign: "The man I kiss is the one you want. Arrest {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.R: Judas had given them a sign so they would know which man was Jesus. He had said, "The man I kiss is the one you want. Arrest {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

decisions.choice: kiss: the usual greeting of a disciple for his teacher
decisions.reason: A kiss was an ordinary sign of respect. In the dark and among many disciples, the armed band needed a way to know Jesus.

decisions.choice: had given: the sign was arranged beforehand
decisions.reason: The Greek past tense here describes something done earlier.

decisions.choice: so they would know which man was Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says what the sign was for.

source.text: καὶ εὐθέως προσελθὼν τῷ Ἰησοῦ εἶπεν· Χαῖρε, ῥαββί· καὶ κατεφίλησεν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately having come to the Jesus he said, Greetings, rabbi, and kissed him.

en.L: And immediately coming up to Jesus, he said, "Greetings, Rabbi!" and kissed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Judas went straight to Jesus and said, "Greetings, Rabbi!" Then he kissed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Judas went right up to Jesus and said, "Hello, Teacher!" Then he kissed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: kissed him: perhaps kissed him warmly
decisions.reason: The verb is a stronger form of the one in 26:48. It may only mean that he carried out the sign.

decisions.choice: Rabbi: as in 26:25
decisions.reason: Judas again uses the title the others avoid.

decisions.choice: Hello, Teacher
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday greeting and gives the title's meaning, as in 26:25.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἑταῖρε, ἐφ’ ὃ πάρει.

records.literal_gloss: The and Jesus said to him, Friend, for what you are here.

en.L: And Jesus said to him, "Friend, [do] that for which you have come."
en.B: Jesus said to him, "Friend, get on with what you are here for."
en.R: Jesus said to him, "Friend, do what you came here to do."

decisions.choice: for what you are here: a command, "do what you came to do"
alternatives: a question: Friend, why are you here?
an exclamation: what you have come for!
decisions.reason: The Greek is short and unfinished. It is most likely a command, but the older reading as a question is possible.

decisions.choice: friend: companion, said with a note of reproach
decisions.reason: Matthew uses this word only when someone is in the wrong (20:13; 22:12).

source.text: τότε προσελθόντες ἐπέβαλον τὰς χεῖρας ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἐκράτησαν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Then having come they laid the hands on the Jesus and seized him.

en.L: Then they came and laid hands on Jesus and seized {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: At that, the crowd moved in. They laid hands on Jesus and arrested {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Then the men came and grabbed Jesus. They arrested {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: laid hands on: took hold of by force
decisions.reason: Here the phrase means to seize someone.

source.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ εἷς τῶν μετὰ Ἰησοῦ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἀπέσπασεν τὴν μάχαιραν αὐτοῦ καὶ πατάξας τὸν δοῦλον τοῦ ἀρχιερέως ἀφεῖλεν αὐτοῦ τὸ ὠτίον.

records.literal_gloss: And behold, one of those with Jesus having stretched out the hand drew the sword of him and having struck the slave of the high priest cut off of him the ear.

en.L: And look, one of those with Jesus stretched out [his] hand and drew his sword, and striking the slave of the high priest, he cut off his ear.
en.B: One of the men with Jesus reached for his sword and drew it. He struck the high priest's servant and cut off his ear.
en.R: One of Jesus's followers pulled out his sword. He struck the high priest's servant and cut off the man's ear.

decisions.choice: one of those with Jesus: Matthew does not name him
decisions.reason: John 18:10 says it was Peter and names the slave Malchus.

decisions.choice: slave: a slave in the high priest's household
decisions.reason: He belonged to the high priest and was probably acting for him.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: τότε λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀπόστρεψον τὴν μάχαιράν σου εἰς τὸν τόπον αὐτῆς, πάντες γὰρ οἱ λαβόντες μάχαιραν ἐν μαχαίρῃ ἀπολοῦνται·

records.literal_gloss: Then says to him the Jesus, Return the sword of you into the place of it; all for those having taken sword by sword will perish.

en.L: Then Jesus says to him, "Put your sword back into its place; for all who take [the] sword will perish by [the] sword.
en.B: Then Jesus told him, "Put your sword back where it belongs. Everyone who takes up the sword will die by the sword.
en.R: Then Jesus said to him, "Put your sword away! People who use swords to fight will be killed with swords.

decisions.choice: all who take the sword will perish by the sword: violence brings violence in return
decisions.reason: A proverb. Compare Genesis 9:6.

decisions.choice: put your sword back: Jesus refuses to be defended by force
alternatives: he forbids all use of force
decisions.reason: He has taught his disciples not to repay evil with evil (5:39), and he goes to his death willingly (26:53-54).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

source.text: ἢ δοκεῖς ὅτι οὐ δύναμαι παρακαλέσαι τὸν πατέρα μου, καὶ παραστήσει μοι ἄρτι πλείω δώδεκα λεγιῶνας ἀγγέλων;

records.literal_gloss: Or do you think that not I am able to call upon the Father of me, and he will provide me now more than twelve legions of angels?

en.L: Or do you think that I cannot call on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will at once provide {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} more than twelve legions of angels?
en.B: Do you not know that I could ask {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would send {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} more than twelve legions of angels right away?
en.R: You know I could ask {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father for help. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would send {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} more than twelve armies of angels right away!

decisions.choice: legions: Roman army units of about six thousand men
decisions.reason: Twelve legions would be more than seventy thousand, a vast host of angels, more than one legion for each of the twelve disciples.

decisions.choice: Jesus could be rescued but chooses not to be
decisions.reason: He goes to his death of his own will, so that the Scriptures may be fulfilled (26:54).

decisions.choice: armies
decisions.reason: Readable explains the military word.

decisions.choice: Do you not know (B); You know (R)
alternatives: Or do you think that I cannot
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the negative question into a direct claim with the same force.

source.text: πῶς οὖν πληρωθῶσιν αἱ γραφαὶ ὅτι οὕτως δεῖ γενέσθαι;

records.literal_gloss: How then would be fulfilled the Scriptures that thus it must happen?

en.L: How then would the Scriptures be fulfilled, that it must happen this way?"
en.B: But if I did, how could the Scriptures come true? They say that all this has to take place."
en.R: But if I did that, what the Scriptures say would not come true. They say these things must happen."

decisions.choice: it must happen: God's plan, written in the Scriptures
decisions.reason: "Must" speaks of God's will, as in 16:21.

decisions.choice: But if I did
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "then" refers back to.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
alternatives: How then would the Scriptures be fulfilled?
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer that they would not; Readable states it.

source.text: ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοῖς ὄχλοις· Ὡς ἐπὶ λῃστὴν ἐξήλθατε μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων συλλαβεῖν με;

records.literal_gloss: In that the hour said the Jesus to the crowds, As against a robber you came out with swords and clubs to capture me?

en.L: At that hour Jesus said to the crowds, "Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs, to capture {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?
en.B: Then Jesus said to the crowd, "Am I some bandit, that you come out with swords and clubs to seize {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?
en.R: Then Jesus said to the crowd, "Why do you come out with swords and clubs to arrest {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? Do you think I am a dangerous criminal?

decisions.choice: robber: a bandit, an armed outlaw
decisions.reason: The word is used of violent robbers and sometimes of rebels. Jesus is crucified between two such men (27:38).

decisions.choice: a dangerous criminal
decisions.reason: Readable gives the force of the word.

source.text: καθ’ ἡμέραν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἐκαθεζόμην διδάσκων καὶ οὐκ ἐκρατήσατέ με.

records.literal_gloss: Every day in the temple I was sitting teaching and not you seized me.

en.L: Every day I sat in the temple teaching, and you did not seize {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.B: Day after day I sat teaching in the temple courts, and you did not arrest {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} then."
en.R: Every day I sat in the temple courtyard and taught the people. You did not arrest {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} then."

decisions.choice: I sat teaching: teachers sat to teach
decisions.reason: As in 5:1 and 13:2. He had taught openly in the temple courts (21:23).

decisions.choice: then
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the contrast with now.

source.text: τοῦτο δὲ ὅλον γέγονεν ἵνα πληρωθῶσιν αἱ γραφαὶ τῶν προφητῶν.

records.literal_gloss: This but all has happened that may be fulfilled the Scriptures of the prophets.

en.L: But all this has taken place so that the Scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled.
en.B: All this took place so that what the prophets wrote in the Scriptures would come true.
en.R: All of this happened to make the words of the prophets in the Scriptures come true.

decisions.choice: the narrator's comment, outside Jesus's speech
alternatives: the end of Jesus's words to the crowd
decisions.reason: The words can be read as Jesus's own (compare Mark 14:49). They are close to Matthew's own comments in 1:22 and 21:4, so the quotation closes before them.

decisions.choice: the Scriptures of the prophets: the prophetic writings as a whole
decisions.reason: Matthew does not name one passage; compare 26:31 and 26:54.

source.text: τότε οἱ μαθηταὶ πάντες ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἔφυγον.

records.literal_gloss: Then the disciples all having left him fled.

en.L: Then all the disciples left {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and fled.
en.B: At that, every one of the disciples abandoned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and ran off.
en.R: Then all the followers left {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and ran away.

decisions.choice: the disciples fled: the scattering foretold in 26:31
decisions.reason: The sheep scatter when the shepherd is struck, as Jesus said.
